title: Afterburner shift notebook
content:
Purpose: quick personal-oncall scratchpad for tonight's handoff. Lightweight, intentionally informal. Use this to scribble actions, temporary fixes, and things to formalize into the official runbook later.

Context: late EMERGENCY window after deploy v2.7.3 that touched batching/kvcache heuristics. We saw a short latency tail spike around 03:10 UTC that tripped the paging threshold for redwood-h2 route. This doc captures my immediate checks, mitigation attempts, and follow-ups.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Incident: increased p95/p99 token latency for hosted-api redwood-h2 route (~220ms -> 1100ms).
- Immediate mitigations: turned on aggressive fallback routing to redwood-h2-compat-1 (cheaper quantized variant), temporarily bumped route concurrency limit down to 6, drained one model-worker pod (rolling restart).
- Current status: metrics trending back to normal but KV cache hit rate degraded ~12% during spike. Observability dashboard shows dropped batching efficiency.

Quick checks (order I ran):
1) Alerts: PagerDuty -> ONCALL-457 (priority P1) — acknowledged.
2) Dashboards: open Console -> per-route latency -> redwood-h2. Confirmed p95/p99 spike at 03:10 UTC.
3) Logs: grep model-worker logs for "batch wait" and "kv-cache-miss" around 03:00-03:30. Command I used:
   kubectl logs -n prod deployment/model-worker-62c | sed -n '9000,9400p' | rg "batch|kv-cache|fallback"
4) Autoscaler: checked horizontal autoscaler for dedicated pool (saw no scale up; pool at 92% GPU util).
5) Circuit options: inspected routing rules in Console -> found no canary active, but route had 'auto-fallback: conservative' which delayed fallback.

Actions taken (sequence & why):
- T=03:16: set route fallback policy to 'aggressive' for redwood-h2 (manual override) to allow immediate spill to compat variant. Reason: reduce tail latency while investigating root cause.
- T=03:18: lowered concurrency limit for route to 6 (from 12) to reduce batch sizes and cut per-token latency spikes. Side-effect: slightly higher cost per token but reduces p99.
- T=03:22: drained pod model-worker-62c for rolling restart (kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-worker). Rationale: logs showed repeated KV cache rebuild bursts on that worker.
- T=03:35: re-enabled normal fallback policy after p99 stabilized ~<250ms for 10min. Kept concurrency at 8 for extra headroom.

Observations / metrics to follow up:
- KV cache hit rate dropped from 78% -> 66% during spike. Need to see whether a model change (v2.7.3) rebased cache keys or changed prefix behavior.
- Batching efficiency dropped: average tokens-per-batch down 30% during peak. Maybe client request skew changed (longer prompts).
- One worker reported repeated "kv-cache cold-start" logs at high frequency -> possibly due to OOM/killed process or segmentation of KV store on restart.

Short-term TODO (during shift):
- [ ] Watch latency and KV cache charts for next 2 hours (alerts configured at +15% threshold).
- [ ] Leave fallback set to 'aggressive' until morning if p99 is stable but KV hit rate not recovered.
- [ ] Post a short note in #infra-status summarizing changes and that rollback -> not needed currently.
- [ ] If spike recurs, trigger model-pin to older variant (redwood-h2-v2.7.2) as rollback plan. Ticket: ONCALL-459 for rollback plan.

Longer-term follow-ups (add to formal runbook):
- Add a checklist for KV-cache cold start detection and automated mitigation (pre-warm key slices on startup).
- Add a matrix mapping fallback aggressiveness to route SLOs and cost tradeoffs.
- Investigate whether recent batching heuristic change (PR #1342) can be gated by rollout to 10% first.

Notes-to-self (handy commands / snippets):
- Check batching stats: curl -s "https://observability.internal/api/v1/metrics?query=batching_tokens_per_batch{route=\"redwood-h2\"}" | jq
- Restart one worker: kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/model-worker-62c
- Dump recent cache metrics: kubectl exec -n prod svc/kv-metrics -- /usr/local/bin/kv-dump --since 30m > /tmp/kv-dump.txt

Open questions / unresolved:
- Did any customer traffic pattern change coincide with spike? (ask growth & product for any new templates pushed ~03:00-03:15 UTC).
- Is there a correlation with autoscaler behavior? HPA didn't scale — maybe insufficient headroom for instant bursts.
- Why did only some model-workers show KV cold starts? Node affinity? OOM kills? Need SRE infra trace.

Hand-off checklist for next engineer:
- Read this doc.
- Confirm p99 < 300ms for 20 continuous minutes before flipping fallback policy to 'normal'.
- If p99 creeps back above 500ms: revert to pinned variant (redwood-h2-v2.7.2) and notify product + release-engineering.
- If you need to restart more than 2 workers, escalate to ENG on call leads (Diego/Priya) first.

Cleanup tasks to do tomorrow (not urgent for tonight):
- Draft a short post-mortem stub in Confluence with timelines and attach relevant logs.
- File a follow-up ticket for quantized-variant perf tests across representative prompts.
- Add a regression test to CI that runs a small-batch latency sweep for redwood-h2 after deployments.

Random observant notes:
- Coffee status: 1/2 left. Keep cold brew near console.
- Personal: update 'oncall-crib' to include the two new quick commands above.

If anything looks off, call me (Asha) or ping Diego. Leaving mobile reachable but prefer Slack; signal only if PD escalation required.

-- end of notes --
